comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Resolved this by using the `react-devtools` package instead of installing the chrome extension.

1. Exec `yarn add --dev react-devtools`
2. Add `"dev:react-devtools": "react-devtools"` or something like that to the scripts in the package.json
3. Add `<script src="http://localhost:8097"></script>` to the dev version of your renderer index html file
4. Now when you exec `yarn run dev:react-devtools` it will launch the react-devtools server and make the react devtools available in the app window devtools.

comments.body:
Electron does not call `extensions::ProcessManager::MaybeCreateStartupBackgroundHosts` which is why the service worker neither starts nor invokes the `chrome.runtime.onStartup` listener.

This method can only be called once which works well for Chrome, but might not be best for Electron. I'll think about how this can be addressed within Electron.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
I've found a better way to fix this: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50611

It turns out that the service worker was actually started when an extension was loaded into an app for the very first time.  When the same extension was loaded on subsequent app launches, the service worker would no longer start. The PR makes it so that the service worker is started on subsequent app launches, too.

Because the service worker was already being started on the first app launch, I've decided not to add a configuration option for now.

comments.author: participant18
comments.body:
We have the similar issue but for our unpacked extension, where we distribute it ourselves inside our electron wrapper. 

1. We load our unpacked extension
````Electron app loading an unpacked MV3 extension into a per-account Session:
const session = Electron.session.fromPartition(`persist:account-${id}`);
await session.loadExtension(extensionPath); // first install
````

2. Load extension version A: session.loadExtension(pathA) → SW registers, versionId: 4, transitions to running. Works.
3. Bump the extension version on the server, the user clicks "Update" in the app.
4. Our reload path runs:
````
for (const ext of session.getAllExtensions()) {
  session.removeExtension(ext.id);
}
await session.loadExtension(pathB);
````
5. Sometimes, previous versionId: 4 survives, causing extension to work not as expected.

Not all the time, but sometimes it is just not initiating the new service worker for the extension. When checked with service worker listener to get running service workers. I observed that when the issue happens previous service worker session id survives even after remove and reinstall of the extension. We don't have specific workaround for it at the moment, beside closing the browser view and  opening it manually multiple times. 

Electron v36.1.0
Extension - MV3
